newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey sees 1997 budget deficit 2,400 trln lira.
newsitem.headline: Turkey sees 1997 budget deficit 2,400 trln lira.

text.p: Turkish Finance Minister Zekeriya Temizel said on Wednesday the new government expected the budget deficit in 1997 to double to around 2,400 trillion lira compared to a deficit of 1,218 trillion a year earlier.
"A budget deficit of 2,400 trillion lira is expected," Temizel said at a joint news conference with State Minister Gunes Taner to announce the government's economic plans.
Islamist former prime minister Necmettin Erbakan had programmed a balanced budget for 1997, but Temizel reiterated that figures for the first half of the year showed a deficit of 720 trillion lira.
He said budget revenues in the full year were expected to amount to 5,112 trillion lira and expenditure was likely to total 7,510 trillion.
Taner, state minister responsible for the economy, reiterated that the expected deficit made it necessary to plan a supplementary budget in the region of 2,500 trillion lira.
The new secularist coalition took power last week after the collapse of Erbakan's one-year-old, Islamist-led government.
Finance Minister Temizel said domestic debt at the end of June stood at 4,213 trillion lira, while foreign debt totalled $80 billion.
He said annual inflation was likely to reach 75-80 percent in 1997 as a whole, compared with the previous government's target of 65 percent.
The Turkish lira was expected to reach an average rate for 1997 of 147,000-150,000 against the dollar.
